slides.sub: In NJ, a 1- or 2-family home needs a smoke alarm, CO alarm and fire extinguisher certificate before new people move in.

slides.title: It's on the seller
slides.body: NJ's fire code says a 1- or 2-family home can't be sold or occupied by someone new until the local fire official issues this certificate.

slides.title: 10-year sealed batteries
slides.body: Battery smoke alarms have to be the 10-year sealed kind. Hardwired alarms can't be swapped out for battery ones.

slides.title: A CO alarm near the bedrooms
slides.body: Homes with a fuel-burning appliance or an attached garage need a CO alarm within 10 feet of the bedrooms.

slides.label: Fire extinguisher, within
slides.body: of the kitchen, rated at least 2-A:10-B:C. Ask when the seller's inspection is booked. Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.

caption:
Here's a rule you'll wish you knew sooner: in NJ, the seller needs a fire safety certificate before you move in.

NJ's fire code says a 1- or 2-family home can't be sold or occupied by someone new until the local fire official issues a smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and fire extinguisher certificate. Battery smoke alarms have to be the 10-year sealed kind. Homes with a fuel-burning appliance or an attached garage need a CO alarm within 10 feet of the bedrooms. And there has to be a fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen.

Ask when the seller's inspection is booked so it doesn't hold up your move.

Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.
